# Report: `region.fasta` (`>region_002`, 3,000 bp)

**Overall composition:** 3,000 bp, GC = 43.6% (A 887 / T 804 / G 661 / C 648). GC content is locally quite uneven (e.g., 59% over 1401–1700 vs. a 17% AT-rich trough around 1101–1200). Coordinates below are 1‑based, inclusive, on the given (+) strand.

## 1. A single long, convincing protein-coding ORF
- **Coordinates 35–703 (+ strand)**: 669 nt, beginning with an `ATG` at 35 and ending with a `TAA` stop at 701–703 → **222 aa** polypeptide (~24 kDa).
- Translation:
  `MWTVSWLRDMLGESLIQDARAQDLSPEDLLNKKASCVPPGCNGLMTVLDWLTNPWEPYKRGIMIGFDSSMDYAWIYRSILESVALTLKNNYDNMCNEMNHFAKHVIITGGGSNSDLFMQIFADVFNLPARRNAINGCASLGAAINTAVGLGLYPDYATAVDNMVRVKDIFIPIESNAKRYDAMNKGIFKDLTKHTDVILKKSYEVMHGELGNVDSIQSWSNA*`
- A stop-free reading frame of this length is not expected by chance (P ≈ 10⁻⁵), so this is the one high-confidence coding feature in the region. I have no database access here, so I cannot assign it a function or a homolog; it does not show internal repeats or obvious targeting motifs.

## 2. A 61-bp tandem repeat array (the most striking non-coding feature)
- **Coordinates 1343–1769 (+ strand)**: **7 tandem copies of a 61-bp unit** (7 × 61 = 427 bp), with perfect periodicity — copy starts at **1343, 1404, 1465, 1526, 1587, 1648, 1709**.
- All seven copies share an **identical 27-bp leader**, `GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAAC`; the remaining 34 bp of each unit are divergent:
  ```
  1343 GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAAC TCGACAGAACGGCCTCAGTAGTCTCGTCAGGCTCC
  1404 GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAAC ACCTGTTTTCGCAAATCTATGGACTATTGCTATTC
  1465 GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAAC ACGGGCGCACGGAATACAAAGCCGTGTATCTGCTC
  1526 GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAAC ACTGGCTCTGCAACAGCAGCACCCATGACCACGTC
  1587 GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAAC ACGAAATGCTGGTGAGCGTTAATGCCGCAAACACA
  1648 GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAAC ACATTACGCCTTTTTGCGATTGCCCGGTTTTTGCC
  1709 GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAAC ACTCTAAACATAACCTATTATTAATTAATGATTTT
  ```
- **Related, more divergent copies** of the same unit occur upstream: **751–811** (`GGTTATCCCCGCTGACGCGGGGAAC…`) and **812–872** (`GTTTATCCCCGCTGATGCAGGGAAC…`), also spaced 61 bp apart, plus a degenerate vestige near **866–879** (`…GGTTTATCCCTG…`). So this repeat family appears at least twice in the region (a two-copy cluster ~751–872 and a seven-copy cluster ~1343–1769).

## 3. Consequences / caveats
- The repetitive DNA generates **spurious short ORFs on both strands** whose conceptual translations are themselves repetitive (e.g., + strand 1338–1634 and 1576–1758 both give peptide-repeats such as `…LSPLARG…`, `…YPRWRG…`). These are artifacts of translating the repeat, not additional genes.
- The only other ORFs of moderate length are on the + strand (**2068–2316**, 82 aa, ATG→TAG; and **2379–2666**, 95 aa), but stop-free reading frames of ~80–100 codons are expected by chance in a 3 kb sequence and I found no supporting features, so I would treat them as provisional.

## Bottom line
Two things stand out: (i) a **222-aa protein-coding gene at 35–703**, and (ii) a **61-bp tandem repeat family**, present as a 7-copy array at **1343–1769** (conserved 27-bp core `GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAAC`) and as two more divergent copies at **751–811** and **812–872**. The remainder of the sequence (an AT-rich trough ~1101–1200 and various short/stray ORFs) shows nothing else clearly functional. Function of both the ORF product and the repeat cannot be assigned from the sequence alone — a database search of the 222-aa protein and of the repeat unit would be the natural next step.
